sentence: This project studies how bacteria in tumors affect the tumor microenvironment in oral squamous cell carcinoma to predict recurrence.
This project studies how autophagy receptors find potentially toxic structures and cause their degradation in mammalian cells.
This project studies how social environments shape adolescent sleep and how poor sleep contributes to physiological dysregulation linked to chronic disease risk.
This project tests circulating biomarkers combined with imaging features to detect early pancreatic cancer.
This project studies antibody glycosylation and human immune organoids to understand responses to Influenza vaccination and infection.
This project shares its molecular imaging agents and software with others through publications, lectures, and its website.
This project helps a network of cancer immunoprevention researchers manage and share data and resources.
This project tests a computer program that reads CT scans to find calcium deposits in heart arteries and predict heart attacks and strokes.
This project tests small molecules that block the activity of a cancer-promoting gene to find a safe cancer therapy.
This project studies how HIV hides in infected microglial cells in the brain, using mice carrying human microglial cells and immune cells.
This project builds an integrated circuit that amplifies and digitizes many neural signals from electrode arrays.
This project studies how enteric glial cells help colon cancer resist chemotherapy.
This project studies how cancer therapies lead to clonal hematopoiesis and how it affects cardiovascular disease in cancer survivors.
This project runs cancer trials on screening, prevention, treatment and cancer care delivery through community partnerships.
This project builds a system that makes genetic information a routine part of clinical medicine, working with doctors and patients.
This project studies the cellular and molecular role of transcription factors in the development of the musculo-skeletal system using human in vitro models.
This project studies different cell types in the inferior colliculus to find how they contribute to hearing.
This project identifies weak interactions in proteins and tests their roles in protein structure and function.
This project tests how a medication that modulates the immune system affects blood vessel inflammation and clonal hematopoiesis.
This project uses mouse models and patient-derived organoids to study how neuroendocrine bladder cancer starts, changes cell type, and responds to chemotherapy.
